classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied rise-and-run diagram to identify the angle to the horizontal and apply inverse tangent to 3/10.

content.prompt:
A road rises at a grade of 3 in 10.
Find the angle (to the nearest degree) the road makes with the horizontal.

spec.description: Road slopes down from upper left to lower right above a horizontal baseline. The vertical left side is labelled 3 and the horizontal base 10. No angle label or right-angle marker is supplied.
spec.mathematics: The requested angle is at the lower-right vertex; opposite-to-adjacent ratio is 3/10.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the angle value is withheld.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the angle the road makes with the horizontal. The opposite side is 3 and the adjacent side is 10.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta &= \frac{O}{A}\\\tan\theta &= \frac{3}{10}\\\theta &= \tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{3}{10}\right)\\\theta &\approx 17^{\circ}\quad\text{(nearest degree)}\end{align*}$$
